col.pullsHint: Cumulative docker pulls recorded by Harbor. A long-standing 0 means no environment uses this image

dialog.desc: Connect a Harbor instance to see project quotas, images and push activity.
dialog.testAfterSave: Saving only means the configuration was stored. A wrong address, an expired password or a disabled account only surface the next time data is actually fetched — so run "Test connection" right after saving.

empty.noSource: Use “Connect registry” on this page to add a Harbor endpoint; quotas and repositories then show live.
empty.title: No image registry connected

emptyRepos.reason: The project exists but nothing has been pushed yet.
emptyRepos.title: No repositories in this project

error.projects: Could not load project quotas (Harbor may be unreachable)

field.envHint: Distinguishes multiple registries, e.g. prod / uat. Optional.
field.envLoadFailed: Failed to load the environment dictionary; only "Any" is selectable
field.name: Name
field.passwordHint: Prefer a read-only robot account over an administrator.
field.skipVerifyHint: Only tick this when Harbor uses a self-signed certificate. It also lets a man-in-the-middle through — be clear about that cost.
field.urlHint: The Harbor address including scheme. A wrong port simply reads as "cannot connect", with no more detail.

liveNote: Queried live from Harbor; nothing is stored
publicHint: Public projects allow anonymous image pulls. Confirm this is intentional — otherwise anyone can pull these images.
staleHint: Not pushed for a long time does not mean it is safe to delete — a rollback may depend on an old tag.
title: Image registry
usedUnknownHint: Storage usage requires admin permission (/quotas), while a robot account is the recommended way to connect Harbor — that is the correct setup. ⚠️ Not readable does NOT mean the project is empty: the repository count on the right is real.
